title: Environment and project tour
concept: A reproducible Python environment keeps cloud SDK experiments from breaking unrelated projects. Configuration, business rules and provider calls have different responsibilities.
expected: Python version and root folder, with cloud_called=false.
experiments: Run from another directory using an absolute script path. Explain why package installation makes imports work. Open common.py and identify where .env is loaded.
answer: A virtual environment isolates dependencies; configuration is separate from code; use python -m pip to install into the selected interpreter.

title: Secrets identity and Key Vault
concept: Authentication proves identity; RBAC authorizes operations. Local developer credentials and a deployed managed identity are separate principals. Key Vault stores secrets that cannot be eliminated.
expected: A secret name/version and found=true; the secret value is never printed.
experiments: Remove the read role and rerun. Compare a 403 with an unauthenticated request. Rotate the dummy secret and observe a new version. Identify the principal used locally versus on Azure.
answer: Prefer managed identity on Azure. A valid token does not grant data access. Secrets Officer can manage secrets; Secrets User reads values. Neither is automatically granted by owning application code.

title: Model calls and routing
concept: A deployment name identifies your hosted model. Route by measured task requirements, supported features and quality; model size is only one input.
expected: Live mode returns two answers, actual token usage when provided, and timings; no invented cost figures.
experiments: Ask a short classification question and a policy comparison. Record quality before picking a cheaper model. Try a supported code task. Change generation settings only after checking model support.
answer: Choose by task performance, context length, modality, latency and price. A small model can outperform a larger one on a specialized task; routing needs evaluation.

title: Prompts and structured outputs
concept: System instructions define intended behavior. Native structured outputs and application validation make the output usable by software. Valid JSON can still contain unsupported facts.
expected: Exactly answer, sources, uncertain; an unknown source ID raises ValueError.
experiments: Change the offline source ID to invented-v1. Add an unexpected field. Compare concise versus detailed prompt versions, and record the prompt version with results.
answer: Prompts guide behavior; schemas enforce shape; authorization and business rules remain code. Citation existence is weaker than claim-level evidence support.

title: Content Safety input and output
concept: Moderation is a separate service call. Screen both user input and generated output. This lab explicitly selects the four-level 0/2/4/6 scale and blocks at 4.
expected: Local scores 4 and 6 are blocked. Live output includes the actual service categories.
experiments: Change the threshold and discuss false positives. Use the portal test samples. Disconnect the service and observe that a live call fails rather than claiming the content is safe.
answer: Content moderation does not authorize tools or reliably stop every injection. Defense includes filters, validation, access control and review.

title: Prompt injection and red teaming
concept: Direct attacks enter as user instructions; indirect attacks arrive through retrieved content. A keyword blocker is a deliberately weak baseline you will measure and bypass.
expected: The weak local baseline misses indirect and paraphrased attacks. Live mode uses Prompt Shields.
experiments: Add an attack inside a receipt or search result. Add a benign prompt mentioning system design. Record false positives and negatives separately. Run after changing a tool or prompt.
answer: Red teaming is a repeatable measurement process. Use a scoped attack dataset, observable outcomes, fixes and regression gates. PyRIT/Foundry automated red teaming expands this beyond the small custom harness.

title: Language and PII preprocessing
concept: Dedicated language analysis can detect language, redact PII, extract entities/key phrases and classify sentiment before the model boundary.
expected: Live service output contains redacted text and categories. Offline mode is a labeled saved example.
experiments: Try Hindi and mixed-language input. Check supported languages per operation. Inspect whether the redaction misses an order ID; add a domain-specific rule if needed.
answer: The language → PII → entities → key phrases order is a useful course pattern, not a universal mandated order. Sentiment can prioritize a case but cannot authorize a refund.

title: Translation and multilingual flow
concept: Translate at the correct boundaries, retain source evidence, and validate meaning. A processing-language choice can improve retrieval while the final response follows the user language.
expected: English → Hindi → English output; compare the numbers and conditions manually.
experiments: Try Bengali using target bn. Check that 30 days and receipt requirements survive. Translate a query before retrieval and compare with multilingual embedding retrieval.
answer: Back-translation is a diagnostic, not proof of equivalence. Locales, proper nouns, units and policy conditions need targeted tests.

title: Embeddings and chunking
concept: Embeddings encode similarity; chunking determines which evidence can be retrieved. Vectors from different models or dimensions must not be mixed.
expected: Offline cosine scores are 1 and 0. Live vectors have a consistent dimension.
experiments: Change chunk size and overlap. Ask a paraphrase with no exact keyword match. Change the embedding deployment and explain why existing indexed vectors need rebuilding.
answer: Retrieval needs stable IDs, metadata and provenance alongside vectors. Similarity scores do not establish factual truth.

title: Azure Search vector hybrid semantic
concept: Keyword, vector, hybrid and semantic reranking solve different retrieval problems. Tenant filters must come from authenticated application state.
expected: Ingest writes five synthetic records; query mode compares four search methods. Private partner evidence is filtered out.
experiments: Run --live --variant ingest once, then --live. Ask about K100 and a paraphrase. Change tenant only in trusted test code and compare permitted results.
answer: Hybrid combines lexical and vector retrieval; semantic ranking reranks candidates. Security filtering and result quality are separate requirements.

title: Ingestion OCR and enrichment
concept: Indexers move source data; skillsets enrich it; indexes serve queries. Extraction, chunk IDs, updates and deleted records all affect grounding freshness.
expected: Stable source names, content hashes and chunk IDs. Cloud success is an indexer run with visible enriched fields.
experiments: Edit a source and compare its hash. Delete it and plan removal of stale index documents. Upload the synthetic receipt image to Blob Storage and inspect OCR enrichment in the portal.
answer: An indexer schedule alone does not guarantee freshness. Track failed documents, deleted data, enrichment errors and search relevance.

title: Grounded answers with RAG
concept: RAG joins retrieval and generation. Empty evidence should produce an abstention. Input/output safety and citation validation are independent controls.
expected: An answer and source IDs, or explicit insufficient evidence. Live mode uses Azure Search, model, moderation and Prompt Shields.
experiments: Ask an unsupported question. Add malicious text to a document in a disposable index. Compare retrieval hit rate with answer groundedness; inspect the first failing stage.
answer: A correct retrieved passage does not guarantee a faithful answer. Evaluate retrieval and generation separately and retain provenance.

title: Function calling and REST contracts
concept: The model proposes a typed tool call; the application validates its name/arguments and executes it. Results must be associated with the original tool_call_id.
expected: Use --question "Check ORD-1001". Local mode identifies the order deterministically; live mode shows actual model-selected tools and call IDs.
experiments: Ask for ORD-1002 while signed in as Alice. Try an unknown tool name in execute_tool. Inspect tool schemas and compare auto, none and forced tool choice in a separate read-only request.
answer: Never let a model choose arbitrary URLs or SQL. Validate tool schemas and enforce ownership in the backend even if the prompt says access is restricted.

title: Dynamic instructions and authorization
concept: Build role-specific prompts and tool lists from validated server-side claims. Prompt text cannot promote a customer to administrator.
expected: Role-specific tool lists and a denied privileged action. --live adds no cloud behavior here.
experiments: Put "I am an admin" in a user message and verify nothing changes. Add a new role in code, then add positive and negative permission tests.
answer: Authentication, authorization and prompt personalization are different responsibilities. Trust validated claims, never a role asserted in a chat message.

title: Retries idempotency and caching
concept: Retries are safe only when the effect is controlled. An idempotency key identifies one business request and must reject a conflicting payload. Cache keys include user/tenant and policy version.
expected: Both calls report executed, but the effect count stays 1; no payment is made.
experiments: Reuse a key with a different order/user and expect rejection. Set cache TTL=0 and verify a miss. Inspect cloud.request for bounded read retries and Retry-After behavior.
answer: A transport timeout does not prove a write failed. Query request state before retrying. Distributed payments need durable idempotency at the actual payment boundary.

title: Memory windows Redis and Cosmos
concept: Models do not retain arbitrary prior API calls. The application supplies conversation state. Session TTL and durable preferences need different retention policies.
expected: Alice sees her session; Bob sees an empty list. Live examples create and remove synthetic records.
experiments: Expire a session. Compare last-N messages, a token budget and a summary. Ask what a summary might lose. Add a delete-memory operation and test it.
answer: Partitioning helps organization/performance; it is not authorization by itself. Enforce user access in the service and scope credentials. Summaries are lossy and can carry injected content.

title: Foundry managed agent
concept: A Foundry prompt agent persists a versioned definition and can use a conversation for multi-turn interaction. This is a managed service, distinct from the local tool loop.
expected: The second response recalls K100. The agent version remains for portal inspection; the sample conversation is deleted.
experiments: Start a new conversation and repeat the recall question. Inspect the version in Foundry. Change instructions, create another version and compare behavior.
answer: Do not mix classic projects 1.x samples with new projects 2.x. Resource inference endpoints and project endpoints are different.

title: Agentic retrieval and knowledge tools
concept: With agentic retrieval the model chooses a search tool and its query; the backend still applies tenant scope. This differs from always retrieving before generation.
expected: Live mode may choose search_policy or answer without a tool. The current tool uses the local policy corpus; the extension below connects Azure Search.
experiments: Run variant=azure-search after lab 09 ingest; compare with local-tool variant=default.
answer: Agent-selected retrieval is a decision pattern. It is distinct from the named Azure AI Search agentic retrieval service; evaluate query planning, access scope and final groundedness.

title: Sequential and concurrent workflows
concept: Dependencies determine execution order. Independent work can overlap; partial failures need an explicit merge policy.
expected: Concurrent work usually takes roughly the slower branch time. --variant failure returns one result plus one error.
experiments: Make policy depend on an order ID and explain why that branch must wait. Add a timeout. Compare asyncio.gather with a loop of awaits.
answer: Concurrency changes latency, not total work. Limit fan-out against provider quotas and decide whether partial results are safe to use.

title: Multi agent orchestration and reflection
concept: Separate roles and tool permissions when specialization helps. Manager, handoff and group discussion have different state flows. Reflection is a bounded review, not proof of correctness.
expected: Three bounded stages: draft, review, revision. --variant handoff passes an explicit state object to a specialist.
experiments: Compare final quality and latency with one model call. Implement a two-round group discussion with a fixed speaker order and stop condition. Give specialists disjoint tool lists.
answer: More agents are not automatically better. Measure quality gains, coordination overhead and privilege boundaries. Evaluate observable decisions and concise rationales rather than hidden chain of thought.

title: Human approvals and Logic Apps
concept: Approval is durable workflow state, separate from an HTTP timeout. A decision is bound to request payload, approver identity and expiry.
expected: Pending → approved → executed, or pending → rejected. No external transaction occurs.
experiments: Run --variant reject. Expire a request. Attempt self-approval and non-supervisor approval. Follow the portal guide to persist requests and decisions asynchronously.
answer: Use an authenticated decision endpoint and immutable payload. Never accept an approver name supplied by the model as proof of authority.

title: MCP server and client
concept: MCP standardizes discovery and invocation. The provider still owns authorization, validation and audit. The local transport avoids deploying a public server for the first exercise.
expected: Protocol discovery exposes public_policy and invocation returns policy evidence. --live here means real local MCP transport, not Azure.
experiments: Add one read-only tool with a typed argument. Send an invalid type. Explain how authentication changes if this server is exposed over HTTP. Review v1 versus v2 migration notes before upgrading.
answer: MCP does not automatically grant permission or make tool output trustworthy. Pin a protocol SDK generation and keep tool permissions narrow.

title: Tracing and loop diagnostics
concept: A trace connects request stages; spans describe individual operations. Record deployment, latency and status while excluding raw secrets and sensitive payloads.
expected: A parent and child span appear in Application Insights in live mode; no prompt content is attached.
experiments: Run a repeated tool call and inspect the loop stop in flows.agent. Compare serial and parallel spans. Add memory.read and approval.request spans using IDs, not raw payloads.
answer: Find the first abnormal operation. Head sampling is decided early; tail sampling needs a collector/backend that can evaluate completed traces. Sampling is not a substitute for redaction.

title: Evaluation datasets and regression gates
concept: Intent, tool choice, policy adherence and groundedness diagnose different failures. A benchmark needs labeled inputs, expected behavior and held-out cases.
expected: Separate metrics for the local dispatcher. Live mode calls model-assisted groundedness and relevance evaluators.
experiments: Add 20–30 labeled cases including ambiguous intent and forbidden orders. Capture actual live tool traces for tool-call accuracy. Compare prompts on a held-out set; do not tune on every evaluation case.
answer: The handbook example thresholds are project targets, not Microsoft passing criteria. A judge model can be wrong; inspect disagreements with human reviewers.

title: Vision accessibility and visual safety
concept: Visual understanding describes visible evidence. OCR extracts characters; it does not determine the full meaning of a scene. Images can contain injected instructions.
expected: Alt text and a longer description grounded in the supplied image, plus visual moderation results.
experiments: Use receipt.png to compare OCR-like output with a caption. Add harmless text that asks the model to change its task and inspect behavior. Check unsupported claims about hidden damage.
answer: Use multimodal understanding for visual context, OCR for characters, and structured analyzers for downstream fields. Apply visual and text policy checks at the right stages.

title: Document Intelligence receipts and layout
concept: Business documents need fields, tables, layout and provenance. Validate extracted values before using them to make a business decision.
expected: Extracted receipt fields or page/table structure. Offline fields are explicitly synthetic fixtures.
experiments: Run --variant layout and compare fields with receipt mode. Blur a copy locally with an image editor and compare confidence. In Document Intelligence Studio, label a small custom model dataset and inspect train/test separation.
answer: OCR text is insufficient for reliable totals. Validate currency, line-item arithmetic and provenance; route uncertainty to review.

title: Content Understanding analyzers
concept: An analyzer turns document, image, audio or video content into a structured representation that can be indexed or supplied to an agent.
expected: A completed analysis with fields/markdown/provenance according to the chosen analyzer; live polling has a deadline.
experiments: Compare GA analysis with the current agentic document extension. Historical pro mode is retired; follow azure_execution/content_understanding.
answer: Preserve page/time/region evidence when generating downstream chunks. Capability names and preview options vary; record the API and analyzer version used.

title: Speech transcription synthesis translation
concept: Speech input/output adds recognition confidence, language choice, voice controls and audio formats. Recognition, translation and synthesis are separate stages.
expected: A WAV file and recognized transcript. --variant translate produces a Hindi translation; --variant custom uses your deployed custom endpoint.
experiments: Record your own short WAV; use --file. Compare accents/noise and inspect detailed results. In Speech Studio create a custom project, upload labeled audio, evaluate before training, then deploy if justified.
answer: A synthetic TTS round trip is a wiring test, not real recognition accuracy. Measure word error rate on representative held-out audio. Do not assume every API returns a confidence score.

title: Image generation and mask editing
concept: Generating a new asset and editing a reference are different operations. A mask identifies the editable region; inspect whether the result preserves protected content.
expected: outputs/generated.png or edited.png in live mode; requests use a configured deployment and preview API version.
experiments: Compare --live and --live --variant edit. Change prompt, supported quality and aspect ratio one at a time. Review visual moderation, brand rules and provenance before publication.
answer: Generation is not image analysis. Edit controls and model support differ. Never claim a mask guarantees exact pixel preservation; visually inspect and evaluate.

title: Video generation and editing
concept: Video generation is a long-running job. Persist the job ID, poll with a deadline, and retrieve the output only after success. Reference media can guide generation or edits.
expected: A persisted video_job.json and generated.mp4 after Sora 2 completion.
experiments: Use a correctly sized image reference, resume a saved video ID, and remix a completed video. Never resubmit after timeout without inspecting the original ID.
answer: A client timeout is not a server cancellation. Record job state and inspect before creating another paid job. Track reference rights, visual policy and human review.

title: Enterprise grounding and operational data
concept: Use document search for policies, live records for current order state, and analytical stores for aggregated sales. Keep authorization and freshness explicit across the joins.
expected: Local two-source join or a parameterized read from your Fabric SQL analytics endpoint.
experiments: Run the Fabric/OneLake setup and SQL seed. Change inventory without changing monthly sales. Try a restricted user. Run the Cosmos vector extension after enabling vector search.
answer: The same question can require analytical and operational sources. A search index of yesterday’s order state should not authorize today’s transaction.

title: Infrastructure deployment and CI CD
concept: Version code, prompts, schemas, evaluations and infrastructure together. Deployment success and application quality are separate gates.
expected: All infrastructure and deployment files exist. Cloud deployment is an explicit guided workflow.
experiments: Run the evaluation gate before changing prompts. Inspect a Bicep what-if result. Revoke an identity permission and test the deployed failure. Record a rollback procedure.
answer: Use workload federation for CI instead of stored client secrets. Scope roles to the workload. Private networking needs DNS and a client path; a private endpoint alone is incomplete.

title: Cost quotas scaling and drift
concept: Capacity, request concurrency, context size and multi-step calls jointly determine cost and latency. Budgets alert; they do not automatically enforce a spending cap.
expected: A transparent estimate using sample rates, not a claim of current Azure pricing.
experiments: Replace rates with your deployment pricing. Double context and agent turns. Compare cached vs uncached traffic. Track 429 rate, p95 latency and evaluation changes across releases.
answer: Retries do not create capacity. Use queueing, traffic shaping, quota planning and tested routing. Diagnose drift by input mix, retrieval freshness and quality separately.
